svg.title: USB Speaker-Mic Converter — confirmed QHM22D dual-PTT wiring
svg.desc: Clean redraw of Adam Fourney's hand-drawn wiring diagram. A two-port USB hub connects a soundcard and an Adafruit KB2040. Soundcard left audio drives an LM386 module and an 8-ohm speaker through the 2.5 mm tip. The 2.5 mm sleeve is common ground. The 3.5 mm ring carries microphone audio, sleeve connects PTT1 to D2, and tip connects PTT2 to D3. Both PTT signals have independent 10 kilohm pull-ups to regulated 3.3 volts. Both switches close to ground. Amplifier power is USB 5 volts or optional boosted 9 volts. This shows functional connections, not physical connector pad order.
svg.text: QHM22D dual PTT · USB audio · LM386 amplifier · KB2040
Functional connections · not physical pin order
Screw terminals at left · input header at right
USB 5 V supplies the hub, soundcard and KB2040 USB power input. +3V3 comes from the KB2040 3V pin.
Connect +VAMP to USB 5 V, or to the optional 9 V boost output. All GND symbols are electrically connected.
Both switches close to common ground. Each GPIO has its own 10 kΩ pull-up. The 3.5 mm tip is PTT2.
